name: Build a public GitHub release digest and share a one-day BrewPage report

parameters.jsCode: return [{json: {dryRun: true, message: 'Public GitHub reads completed; no BrewPage publish request sent. Review content, choose visibility, acknowledge write-once publishing, then disable dryRun. Expiry: 1 day.', releaseCount: $json.releaseCount, sourceCount: $json.sourceCount, content: $json.body.content, format: 'html'}}];

parameters.content:
## GitHub release digest → one-day report
### How it works
Collect public releases from up to five repositories, filter by date and prerelease preference, remove duplicate links and build a readable HTML digest with source links and shortened release-note excerpts. Preview before sharing a one-day BrewPage link. No AI model, signup or API key is needed.
### Setup
1. Open **Report inputs**; set repositories as `owner/repo`, title and filters.
2. Execute with `dryRun: true`. Public GitHub GETs run; no report is published. Read **Dry run preview → content**.
3. Choose `public` or `unlisted`; anyone with an unlisted link can read it. Set `acknowledgeWriteOnce: true`, then `dryRun: false` and execute once.
4. Copy only **Reader URL only → url**.
### Customize
Change the 1–30 day lookback and up to five matches per repository. Keep TTL at one day. This template is manual; execute again to create a new digest.

## 1 · Choose public sources
Inputs are checked before network reads. One GET per repository fetches its first 20 releases. No authentication or arbitrary URL input. Private, renamed or missing repositories stop execution; use their current public names.

## 2 · Turn releases into a report
Filter drafts, old releases and optional prereleases; sort newest first and deduplicate source links. Remote text is escaped, never rendered as supplied HTML. Empty sources and fetch-limit warnings remain visible.

## 3 · Inspect, then share
Dry run returns HTML plus source/release counts. Live execution requires both access choice and write-once acknowledgement. GitHub reads can occur during preview; only the approved branch sends a BrewPage POST.

## Write-once · expires in one day
Owner capability is not retained. This workflow cannot update or delete the report early. Never share the Publish report response or raw execution output; share only the final reader URL.

## Troubleshooting
GitHub 403/429: wait for its rate limit to reset. 404: check the public repository name. Other failed reads stop publishing. Zero matches produces an explicit empty digest. Only 20 releases per source are checked; this is not a complete release archive.

## Publishing basics — earlier simpler workflow
Illustrated beginner tutorial for importing a report workflow, choosing visibility, acknowledging write-once publishing and sharing only the reader URL. It shows the earlier static-report workflow, not this GitHub digest or live n8n execution. Follow Start here for the new source/filter/preview steps.
